newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money nudges lower despite Buba drain.
newsitem.headline: German call money nudges lower despite Buba drain.

text.p: German call money traded slightly softer on Wednesday as liquidity conditions remained largely in equilibrium, even after the Bundesbank drained funds at its weekly securities repurchase award.
Dealers said overnight funds traded between 3.05/10 percent on Wednesday, down slightly from Tuesday's 3.08/10 percent rates. The bulk of trades were conducted below 3.10 percent.

The Bundesbank this morning drained a net one billion marks from the money market, a move dealers said was not having much of an impact on the market. While the market was "not swimming in funds, the drain could have been bigger," a dealer said.

Banks held 43.4 billion marks in reserve at the Bundesbank on Tuesday compared with 43.6 billion marks held one day earlier. Meanwhile the monthly average rate slipped to 43.7 billion marks from 43.8 billion marks. Lombard borrowings, at the 4.50 percent emergency funding rate, stood at 100 million marks on Tuesday, the Bundesbank said.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was set at 3.10233 percent on Wednesday compared with 3.11100 percent on Tuesday.
